sections.h2: What is a lady bird deed in Florida?
sections.html:
A lady bird deed is a deed that gives an owner a life estate with enhanced powers and names who receives the property afterward. It is also called an enhanced life estate deed, and the Department of Revenue has written about its tax treatment in an advisement dated October 16, 2020.

What matters is the wording of the deed itself: which powers the owner keeps and who the named remainder people are. Two deeds that both get called lady bird deeds can read differently, so the recorded text controls. Read it line by line before you plan a sale.

sections.h2: Does a lady bird deed owe Florida documentary stamp tax?
sections.html:
In the Department of Revenue's advisement TAA 20B4-004, the answer was no, on the facts presented. The department concluded the deed did not transfer any present beneficial interest and was not subject to documentary stamp tax regardless of any consideration.

Those facts mattered. The life tenants in that request kept full powers over the property. A deed that gives up some of those powers could be analyzed differently, and the advisement answered one taxpayer's set of facts. Ask the county clerk of court or a Florida real estate attorney before you record, since the clerk collects the tax at recording.

For comparison, the department's general page lists life estate deeds among taxable deeds, and states that the rate on deeds is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade. The advisement is the reason an enhanced life estate deed can be treated differently from an ordinary life estate deed.

sections.h2: How does a lady bird deed affect selling the home?
sections.html:
A sale starts with a deed to the buyer signed with the formalities Florida requires, so the first question is who must sign.

Section 689.01 requires a conveyance of an interest in land to be in writing and signed in the presence of two subscribing witnesses. A seal is not needed, and witnessing may be done by audio-video technology. Whether the named remainder people must also sign depends on the powers written into your deed, and a title company will read the recorded deed before agreeing to insure. Treat that as a question for the title agent, and raise it before you list the house.

  • Get a certified copy of the recorded deed from the county clerk.
  • Check which powers the deed reserves to the owner, including selling and mortgaging.
  • Ask the title company whether it will insure with only the owner signing.
  • Plan for the sale deed to be taxed at the standard doc stamp rate.

sections.h2: What does it do to property taxes and the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
The tax effect depends on whether a transfer counts as a change of ownership. Under Save Our Homes in section 193.155, any sale, foreclosure or transfer of legal or beneficial title resets the assessment to just value the following January 1, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses and certain transfers upon death.

The Department of Revenue treats the Save Our Homes cap as the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change each year. Its chart shows a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024, when CPI was 3.4 percent. Because the lady bird advisement reasoned that no present beneficial interest passes, ask the county property appraiser how that office classifies your deed before relying on it.

The homestead exemption itself is up to $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to all property taxes, including school taxes, and the additional amount applies only to assessed value over $50,000 for non-school taxes. Apply with Form DR-501 by March 1. The exemption is lost if the unit is rented or stops being the permanent home.

sections.h2: What happens to the homestead benefit if the owner sells and buys again?
sections.html:
The owner can carry part of the Save Our Homes savings to a new Florida home through portability, if the new homestead is established in time. The Department of Revenue says to establish it within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead was abandoned, not three years from the sale date.

File Form DR-501T with the new DR-501 by March 1. Section 193.155(8) reduces the new home's assessed value by the lesser of $500,000 or the gap between just value and assessed value on the old home. The statute page notes that amendments from chapter 2026-239 first apply to the 2027 tax roll, so ask the property appraiser which version applies to your filing year.

  • A sale of the old home is a change of ownership, so the buyer's assessment resets to just value.
  • The homestead application deadline is March 1 of the tax year, filed with the county property appraiser.
  • The owner must make the property the permanent residence by January 1 of that year.
  • Homestead is lost if the unit is rented, stops being the permanent home, or the owner is no longer a Florida permanent resident.

sections.h2: What should a seller compare before choosing a deed?
sections.html:
Compare how each deed type is treated for tax, signing and title insurance, since the differences show up at closing.

Deed typeDoc stamp tax per the Department of RevenueSource
Lady bird (enhanced life estate), on the facts in TAA 20B4-004Not subject, regardless of considerationTAA 20B4-004
Life estate deedListed as a taxable deedDOR doc stamp page
Quit claim deedListed as a taxable deedDOR doc stamp page

Source: Florida Department of Revenue.

Recording costs follow section 28.24: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, $1.00 for each name beyond four, a $1.00 first-page and $0.50 added-page modernization charge, and an extra $4 per page technology charge.

sections.h2: What if the owner wants to sell fast with a lady bird deed in place?
sections.html:
A buyer who pays cash still needs a clean, insurable deed, so gather the recorded deed, the legal description and any mortgage payoff before you speak with buyers.

Expect the closing agent to confirm every signer, collect doc stamp tax on the sale deed at recording, and pay off liens from proceeds. If the owner has died, the deed's terms and any probate steps decide who can sign next, and the title company will tell you which court papers it needs. The clerk of the circuit court records the deed and collects the tax, so questions about recording go to that office.

faqs.q: Is a lady bird deed subject to Florida doc stamp tax?
faqs.a: Not on the facts in Department of Revenue advisement TAA 20B4-004, dated October 16, 2020, where the life tenants kept full powers. The department said no present beneficial interest passed, so no tax applied regardless of consideration. Confirm your own facts with the clerk or an attorney.

faqs.q: Do I need two witnesses on a lady bird deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 689.01 requires a conveyance of an interest in land to be in writing and signed in the presence of two subscribing witnesses. No seal is needed, and the witnessing may be by audio-video technology.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house I hold under a lady bird deed?
faqs.a: Often yes, depending on the powers your deed reserves. Show the title company the recorded deed first. It will tell you whether your signature alone is enough or whether the named remainder people must join.

faqs.q: Does a lady bird deed keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The exemption depends on the home staying your permanent residence, not on the deed type. Renting the home or moving out ends it, and a change of ownership resets the Save Our Homes assessment. Ask the county property appraiser how your deed is classified.

faqs.q: Where do I record a lady bird deed?
faqs.a: Record it with the clerk of the circuit court in the county where the land sits. The clerk collects any documentary stamp tax at recording and charges the page fees set by section 28.24.
